prompt: Why does the course recommend installing Ollama on the computer you use every day rather than in a virtual machine?

choices.text: Ollama will not start inside a virtual machine
choices.why: It starts; inside a VM it runs on the processor only.

choices.text: A VM takes a fixed share of memory and hides the GPU
choices.why: Right. A model wants all the memory and the graphics card it can get.

choices.text: The course's programs only run on the host's own Python
choices.why: The same steps run inside the VM exactly as written.

choices.text: A virtual machine needs a paid licence for the hypervisor
choices.why: VirtualBox and UTM cost nothing; the reason is the computer's resources.

prompt: Ollama ignores the API key. Why does the course set OPENAI_API_KEY at all?

choices.text: The SDK refuses to start without one
choices.why: Right. So it is set to a word that says where it goes.

choices.text: Ollama checks it against an account on ollama.com
choices.why: Ollama asks nobody; it needs no account and ignores the key.

choices.text: It picks which of the downloaded models answers
choices.why: The model is named in every request, not in the key.

choices.text: It encrypts the requests between the SDK and Ollama
choices.why: It is a word sent in a header; it encrypts nothing.

prompt: In releases.json, the similarity below which a chunk is not shown to the model is called the ___.
What does a span record that a log line with a timestamp does not?

choices.text: The model's reply, word for word, with its finish reason
choices.why: A log line can carry the reply as well as a span can.

choices.text: Its parent, and the trace it belongs to
choices.why: Right. The ids are what let a tool rebuild the tree and find every span of one request.

choices.text: The time the operation happened
choices.why: A timestamp is exactly what a log line has.

choices.text: Whether the answer was right
choices.why: Neither does: the span in this section is perfect and the answer is wrong.

prompt: one_call.py's span had status UNSET and finish reason stop, and the reply said the model knew nothing about a Marginalia gift card. What does that show?

choices.text: That the span was written wrongly and the attributes cannot be trusted
choices.why: Every attribute on it is correct. The call did succeed.

choices.text: That the provider returned an error the SDK swallowed without saying
choices.why: An error would have set the status to ERROR; this one is UNSET.

choices.text: That a successful call and a useful answer are different facts
choices.why: Right. The trace records what happened; whether it was right takes evaluation, lessons 8 to 13.

choices.text: That the model ran out of tokens
choices.why: That would show as finish reason length, not stop.

prompt: Match each gen_ai attribute to what it says.

pairs.right: the model the code asked for
how many tokens the reply took
what kind of call it was, such as chat

prompt: A team asks for the alias of a model, and its spans record only gen_ai.request.model. What will they be unable to see?

choices.text: How many tokens each call used, since those are counted per model name
choices.why: Token counts are separate attributes and do not depend on the model name.

choices.text: The day the alias began pointing at a different snapshot
choices.why: Right. Only the response model says which snapshot answered; the request says the same alias every day.

choices.text: Which calls failed
choices.why: Failures are in the span's status, whatever the model attributes say.

choices.text: Which feature made each call
choices.why: That was never in a model attribute; it is the root span's app.feature.

prompt: Put the assistant's steps for an answered question in the order their spans start.
In the return-postage question's trace, how many milliseconds did the chat llama3.2:3b span take?
A trace's root took 900 ms and its children add up to 600 ms, one after the other. What is the first thing to suspect?

choices.text: The clock of the machine is wrong
choices.why: A wrong clock shifts every span alike; it does not open a gap between them.

choices.text: The model was slow
choices.why: A slow model shows as a long chat span, which would be counted among the children.

choices.text: The spans ran in parallel
choices.why: Children in parallel would add up to MORE than the root, not less.

choices.text: Some work runs in code that opens no span
choices.why: Right. Time inside the root that no child covers was spent somewhere nobody instrumented.

prompt: Why does the assistant retry in its own code instead of letting the SDK retry?

choices.text: So that each attempt is a span of its own, with its own error and its own time
choices.why: Right. A retry inside the SDK happens inside one span and leaves no trace of itself.

choices.text: Because the SDK cannot retry
choices.why: It can, and by default it does.

choices.text: Because retrying in Python is cheaper than retrying in the SDK
choices.why: The cost is the same requests either way.

choices.text: To make the answer faster
choices.why: Where the retry lives does not change how long it waits.

prompt: The return-postage answer was wrong. Which attribute cleared the retrieval step of blame?

choices.text: gen_ai.usage.output_tokens = 14, a short reply
choices.why: A short reply is not a wrong one, and says nothing about the search.

choices.text: app.time_to_first_token_ms = 1663, a slow start
choices.why: Time says nothing about which sources the model read.

choices.text: app.search.chunks, naming the section on returns
choices.why: Right. The one chunk the model was given is the one that says returns are free.

choices.text: gen_ai.operation.name = chat, on the model call
choices.why: Every model call here is a chat.

prompt: The student-discount trace has no generate span. What does that tell you?

choices.text: The model read the sources and refused to answer
choices.why: The model was never called. A model's refusal would have a generate span.

choices.text: The trace was cut off before it finished
choices.why: check_citations ran after the missing step, so the request finished.

choices.text: No chunk cleared the floor
choices.why: Right. The refusal came from the code, cost no model tokens, and took 46 ms.

choices.text: The span exporter dropped the span on its way to the file
choices.why: Nothing here drops spans; the step simply did not run.

prompt: Which of these belong on a retrieval span? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: How many results came back
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: How many cleared the floor
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The ids of the chunks kept
choices.why: Right. An id finds the text whenever it is needed.

choices.text: The full text of every chunk returned
choices.why: The ids are enough to find them, and the text is what lesson 2 is careful about.

prompt: Two refusals look the same on screen. One trace has a generate span and one does not. Where is each fixed?

choices.text: Both in the prompt, since a refusal is a sentence the prompt asks for
choices.why: The one without a generate span never reached a prompt.

choices.text: Both in the search, which decides what the model gets to read
choices.why: The one with a generate span got past the search.

choices.text: Neither: a refusal is always right
choices.why: A refusal to a question the documents answer is a wrong answer.

choices.text: One in the search, the other in the prompt or sources
choices.why: Right. One was stopped by the floor; the other read sources and judged they did not answer.

prompt: What did the OpenInference instrumentor record without being asked?

choices.text: Nothing but the duration
choices.why: It recorded far more: the messages, the reply, the tokens.

choices.text: The whole prompt and the whole reply, as attributes on the span, by default
choices.why: Right. It is the default, and lesson 2 is about what that means in production.

choices.text: Only a hash of the prompt, so the text cannot be read back
choices.why: The text is there in input.value and llm.input_messages.

choices.text: The API key
choices.why: No key appears in its attributes.

prompt: OpenInference wrote llm.token_count.prompt; the hand-written span wrote gen_ai.usage.input_tokens. What does the difference mean in practice?

choices.text: A tool must read the names it writes
choices.why: Right. Same fact, two names: which one a tool understands decides whether it sees the tokens at all.

choices.text: They measure different tokens: one counts the prompt and one the whole input
choices.why: Both read the same usage field of the reply.

choices.text: One of them is wrong
choices.why: Both are correct in their own convention.

choices.text: OpenTelemetry forbids the llm prefix
choices.why: Nothing forbids it; it is simply another convention.

prompt: Before the first customer's message goes through a newly installed instrumentation library, what is the one check this lesson asks for?

choices.text: Benchmark its overhead under the traffic of a normal day
choices.why: Worth knowing, but it is not the risk this section is about.

choices.text: Make one call and read the span it writes
choices.why: Right. It shows which convention it uses and whether it keeps the text, in a minute.

choices.text: Read its licence and the list of packages it depends on
choices.why: A licence does not say what the library records by default.

choices.text: Turn off every other exporter
choices.why: The others are not the question; what this one keeps is.

prompt: A thumbs down arrives from the browser a few seconds after a reply. What should it be joined to the reply by?

choices.text: The trace id that came back with the reply, sent along with the click
choices.why: Right. Two requests can share words and a second, never a trace id.

choices.text: The user and the time, to the second, of the last reply they got
choices.why: The same person can ask twice in a minute, and the join lands on the wrong answer.

choices.text: The text of the question
choices.why: Many people ask the same words.

choices.text: The order of arrival
choices.why: Requests overlap; position says nothing about which reply a click is about.

prompt: How many spans did the return-postage trace have in spans.jsonl?
A support screen shows customers the first eight characters of the trace id. What must the screen that opens a trace from it check?

choices.text: Nothing: the id itself is the permission
choices.why: An id is a handle, not a secret, and a trace with the question on it is the conversation.

choices.text: That all 32 characters were typed
choices.why: Length is not access control.

choices.text: Who is asking, and whether they are allowed to see it
choices.why: Right. The same check as for the conversation itself.

choices.text: That the trace is less than a day old
choices.why: Age says nothing about who may read it.

prompt: Match each span of the assistant to what it measures.

pairs.right: turning the question into a vector
the arithmetic over the chunks in the index
the whole request, from question to reply

prompt: A span opened while another is current takes that one as its ___, and that is what turns spans into a tree.
A trace shows a generate span with three chat children, the first two marked as errors. What happened?

choices.text: The model answered three times
choices.why: Two of the three attempts failed; only one could have answered.

choices.text: Three customers asked at once and their spans were merged into one trace
choices.why: Three customers are three traces, each with its own root.

choices.text: The citations were checked three times, once per source in the prompt
choices.why: That would be check_citations spans, not chat spans.

choices.text: The provider refused twice and the third attempt was answered
choices.why: Right. One span per attempt is exactly what the assistant's retry loop writes.

prompt: ollama list answers: could not connect to ollama server. What is wrong?

choices.text: The background service never started, or has stopped
choices.why: Right. The command works; the server it talks to is not there. Start the service, or run ollama serve.

choices.text: The model llama3.2:3b has not been downloaded yet
choices.why: Then the list would come back empty, not fail to connect.

choices.text: The Python environment is not active in this terminal
choices.why: ollama is not a Python program; the environment changes nothing for it.

choices.text: Another program is already listening on the port
choices.why: That is what a second ollama serve says, and it means a server IS running.

prompt: Two of the seven documents can never reach the model. What keeps them out?

choices.text: Their front matter: superseded, and internal
choices.why: Right. The assistant searches only chunks that are current and public.

choices.text: Their similarity is always below the floor
choices.why: Their scores are never computed against a question; they are dropped first.

choices.text: index.py skips them when it builds the index
choices.why: They are in the index; the assistant drops them when it loads it.

choices.text: The model is told in its instructions to ignore them
choices.why: A model can disobey an instruction; these are never sent at all.

prompt: A program stops with openai.APIConnectionError: Connection error, after a pause of a few seconds. Where should you look first?

choices.text: At whether Ollama's server is still running
choices.why: Right. Nothing answered at OPENAI_BASE_URL; ollama list says so in one line.

choices.text: At the API key, which Ollama has started to check
choices.why: Ollama ignores the key; a refused key is an error with a status code.

choices.text: At the model, which ran out of tokens mid-answer
choices.why: That ends with a finish reason, not a failed connection.

choices.text: At the prompt, which is too long for the model
choices.why: A long prompt is answered or refused by a server that is there.
